{{Quote|You know, that ship's saved my life quite a few times. She's the fastest hunk of junk in the galaxy!|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]|<ref name="ESB" />}}
The '''''Millennium Falcon''''', originally known as '''YT-1300 492727ZED''', was a modified [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]] known under various aliases and pseudonyms such as '''''Corell's Pride''', '''Fickle Flyer''', '''Meetyl's Misery''', '''Jackpot''', '''Hardwired''', '''Wayward Son''', '''Stellar Envoy''', '''Second Chance''', '''Gone to Pieces''', '''Close Shave''', '''Sunfighter Franchise''', '''Victory Ring''', '''Belle of Byblos''', '''Longshot''', '''Regina Galas''', '''Sunlight Franchise''',  '''Sweet Surprise''', '''Shadow Bird''', '''Princess of Blood''', '''Star Princess''', '''Star Tripper''', and '''Naboo Duckling''''' with a storied history stretching back to the decades before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Manufactured by the [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] in [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]], the [[Light freighter/Legends|light freighter]] was first owned by [[Corell Industries Limited/Legends|Corell Industries Limited]] and underwent several name changes before being bought by the [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] [[Kal Brigger|Kal]] and [[Dova Brigger]] in [[48 BBY/Legends|48 BBY]], and the ship eventually ended up as the property of the secretive [[Republic Group/Legends|Republic Group]] under the name '''''Stellar Envoy''''' by [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]]. The ''Envoy'' was destroyed in a collision with a [[Bulk freighter/Legends|bulk freighter]] above [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], but it was rebuilt and served various owners under different names before [[Quip Fargil]] named it after the [[bat-falcon]], and it eventually fell into the hands of [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] after a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]]&mdash;but Calrissian himself lost the ship in another game of sabacc to the smuggler [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] several [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later.

Solo and his [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] copilot, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], became the ship's most famous and permanent owners, flying the ''Falcon'' during their smuggling careers and their subsequent work with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]; a fateful trip to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] from [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], ferrying [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Ben Kenobi]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] there, saw Solo and the ''Falcon'' embroiled in the Alliance's affairs and participating in the historic [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]&mdash;during which Solo and Chewbacca flew the ''Falcon'' to save Skywalker from Imperial [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] and allowed him to fire the shot that destroyed the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]]. Despite Solo's insistence that he did not work for the Alliance, his misadventures continued to draw him back to the Rebels and [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], and the ''Falcon'' was present for many pivotal battles of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] such as the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] and the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]&mdash;where Lando Calrissian and his copilot [[Nien Nunb/Legends|Nien Nunb]] flew alongside [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] into the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star's]] superstructure and fired the shots that spelled the massive battle station's [[Battle of Endor/Legends#Final_actions|destruction]]. Solo continued to fly the ship for several decades through a slew of galactic conflicts.

==History==
===The early years===
{{Quote|Flandon's Teeth, what a history that ship has!|[[Milo Thirk]], [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] Bureau Chief, [[Bespin system/Legends|Bespin system]]|<ref name="Sourcebook 1" />}}
The [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]] designated unit YT 492727ZED was built in [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]] by the [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] at [[Orbital Assembly Facility 7/Legends|Orbital Assembly Facility 7]]. While still on the assembly line, an accident with a fuel [[Droid/Legends|droid]] sent the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] rocketing out of control, and the ship almost destroyed the entire assembly line before several workers were able to regain control of the vessel.<ref name="Falcon" /> The ship remained in stock state for several years,<ref name="Polyhedron">{{PolyhedronCite|162|Exposing the YT-1300 Transport: Secrets of the Falcon|Exposing the YT-1300 Transport: Secrets of the ''Falcon''}}</ref> and it was first owned by the [[Corell Industries Limited/Legends|Corell Industries Limited]] shipping firm, who possessed the ship for twelve years and utilized it as a shipping vessel in the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]]. Developing a reputation as a stubbornly unreliable yet remarkably swift vessel, the YT flew under a series of names&mdash;including the ''Corell's Pride'', ''Fickle Flyer'', and ''Meetyl's Misery''&mdash;before CI Limited declared bankruptcy in [[48 BBY/Legends|48 BBY]]. During those twelve years, a number of pilots flew the YT-1300 with varying degrees of success, with one pilot making a run to [[Tralus/Legends|Tralus]] in record time while another was marooned over five hundred [[Meter/Legends|kilometers]] from [[Selonia/Legends|Selonia]] with an entire cargo of defrosting [[plar fish]]. One pilot was able to beat another vessel named the ''[[Fusion Flame]]'' in a race around the planet [[Drall (planet)|Drall]], and every pilot retrofitted and tinkered with the vessel in a series of makeshift repairs and retoolings&mdash;one pilot was forced to install a poorly-built [[pulse generator]], and a later navigator nearly destroyed the ship's [[Fabritech transceiver relay]] with a [[Hydrospanner/Legends|hydrospanner]] when it refused to work.<ref name="Falcon" />

[[File:StellarEnvoy-SWE.png|thumb|left|180px|The ''Stellar Envoy'' during the Clone Wars.]]
As the ''Jackpot'', the ship was sold to [[Kal Brigger|Kal]] and [[Dova Brigger]], and the siblings used the newly rechristened ''Hardwired'' for various and increasingly illicit cargo runs between [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] and other [[Planet/Legends|planets]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. The siblings also upgraded the [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], but the pair's relationship with the [[Smugglers' Confederation]] of the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]] went sour and resulted in Dova's [[Death/Legends|death]]. Kal survived and renamed the ship ''Wayward Son'', changing the ship's registry to [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]], before joining [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark's]] [[Stark Commercial Combine|Commercial Combine]], but he was devoured by the predatory insects known as [[challat eater]]s on [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]] in [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]].<ref name="Falcon" />

In [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]], the vessel was purchased by the [[Republic Group/Legends|Republic Group]], a secretive organization and corporate conglomerate run by members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Tobb Jadak]] and his friend [[Reeze Duurmun]] became the primary crew of the ship, which had been renamed the ''Stellar Envoy'', for the next decade, and the pair made frequent trips to far-flung planets like [[Yinchorr/Legends|Yinchorr]] and [[Ansion/Legends|Ansion]] while also upgrading the ''Envoy''{{'s}} communications systems and hyperdrive.<ref name="Falcon" />

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the ''Stellar Envoy'' was on [[Ongary IX]], which the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] had [[Attack on Ongary IX|invaded]] in search of [[hfredium]]. Leaving the planet for the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] after the battle, Jadak and Duurmun took as a passenger [[Jorn Kulish]]. Kulish was a disgruntled member of the [[Ividal Sector Forces]] who had resigned after a harrowing experience conducting bombing runs during the battle with an opaque [[Blast shield/Legends|blast shield]] fitted to his helmet to stop his eyes being dazzled by the explosion of [[burrowing plasma charge]]s. Demonstrating the helmet and shield to Jadak and Duurmun to illustrate why he resigned, Kulish accidentally left the helmet behind when he disembarked at [[Denon/Legends|Denon]]. The helmet and blast shield would remain in the freighter's hold for decades under a succession of owners until [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] found a use for it in training [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] in the ways of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="Warfare Author's Cut Part 10">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-10-the-rise-of-the-empire|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 10: The Rise of the Empire}}</ref>

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the ship was present during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]], landing at the [[Republic Executive Building/Legends|Republic Executive Building]] docking bay on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] shortly after the shuttle that brought [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], Obi-Wan Kenobi, and [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] to safety<ref name="Falcon" /> after their crash landing in the nose of the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref>

Shortly after this, the ''Stellar Envoy'' was hit by the [[Bulk freighter/Legends|bulk freighter]] ''[[Jendirian Valley III]]'' over [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], causing massive critical damage to the entire frame. Duurmun was killed in the collision while Jadak fell into a coma from which he would not wake for nearly sixty years. What was left of the ship was interned in an orbital junkyard near the Smuggler's Moon. The ship rested there for about a month before it was purchased as scrap by an enterprising technician named [[Bammy Decree/Legends|Bammy Decree]], with assistance from crime lord [[Rej Taunt]]. Under Decree's co-ownership, the ''Envoy'' was reconstructed from core to hull, and various systems were replaced with updated versions. Though the effort purportedly required a great deal of time and effort, the technician committed himself to finish the job as a test of skill, and also perhaps a labor of love. It was during this time that several sections of the ship were refitted with modular components from an old YT-1300p light freighter that had previously been used for diplomatic missions before meeting a similar fate.<ref name="Polyhedron" /> The Imperial Navy's Chief Naval Engineer [[Lira Wessex/Legends|Lira Wessex]] was also involved in the retrofitting/repair of the ''Envoy''.<ref name="TechPlate">[["Millennium Falcon" TechPlate]]</ref><ref name="SpecPlate">[["Millennium Falcon" SpecPlate]]</ref>

Renamed the '''''Second Chance''''', it served its new owners only briefly, performing a single botched smuggling attempt before languishing in Imperial impound at [[Nilash III]] for the next few years. It was then stolen by an opportunistic ship thief, one [[Zenn Bien]], working with [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] agents [[Quip Fargil]] and [[Luufkin]]. The ''Second Chance'' was briefly rechristened the '''''Gone to Pieces''''' during this operation, but when he began flying the ship for the Alliance, he rechristened her the '''''Millennium Falcon''''', after the [[bat-falcon]]<ref name="Falcon" /> &mdash; the name that the ship would carry through the remainder of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] and on through the [[Second Galactic Civil War]] and after.

The ''Falcon'' was to be used in a Rebel strike at [[Bilbringi system/Legends|Bilbringi]] in [[9 BBY/Legends|9 BBY]], but Fargil had second thoughts and pulled out of the operation, taking the ''Falcon'' with him. Unable to live with his guilt, he donated her to Doctor [[Parlay Thorp]]. After spending several years on [[Hijado]] with Thorp, the ''Falcon'' was sold to [[Molpol's Traveling Circus]], and was the collateral of at least a few wagers before coming into the hands of a young [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]. The ship's identiplate was removed during this time to facilitate its new career in [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] by one such owner, and each also added their own "special modifications" so that, by the time it came into the hands of Lando, it was already able to out fly almost any vessel of its size.<ref name="Polyhedron" />

===Smuggling days===
{{Quote|Take good care of her, Solo. That ship saved my life quite a few times over the years.|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]|<ref name="Sourcebook 1" />}}
Lando Calrissian acquired the ''Falcon'' in a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] around [[5 BBY/Legends|5 BBY]] from a certain [[Cix Trouvee]], a professional gambler who couldn't cover his debt.<ref name="Falcon" /> After learning the basics of its controls from his new friend [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], he collaborated with his [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Vuffi Raa]] and operated as a freelance transporter. Calrissian piloted the ship during his smuggling missions in the [[Rafa system/Legends|Rafa system]],<ref name="LCFO">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Mindharp of Sharu]]''</ref> the [[Oseon system/Legends|Oseon belt]],<ref name="LRFO">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Flamewind of Oseon]]''</ref> and the Starcave of [[ThonBoka]].<ref name="LCST">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Starcave of ThonBoka]]''</ref> He continued to make modifications to the ship in order to better protect himself during these runs. During this time, the ''Falcon'' suffered a large tear near its entry ramp when a [[Renatasian Confederation]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] rammed it.

[[File:Sabaccfinal.jpg|thumb|left|The fateful [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] game in which Lando Calrissian lost the ''Falcon'' to Han Solo.]]

During the final round of the [[Cloud City Sabacc Tournament]], Calrissian threw in a marker for "any ship on his lot" (at the time, he was the owner of a used spaceship lot on Nar Shaddaa, where the ''Falcon'' was parked). Solo, the other contestant remaining in the tournament, accepted the marker, knowing that Calrissian had taken a cruise ship to the tournament and left the ''Falcon'' behind. When Solo won the game, he claimed the ''Falcon'' as his own on the technicality which had been overlooked by his unlucky opponent.

After winning the ''Millennium Falcon'' from Calrissian, Solo began to add to the prior owners' modifications. His personal enhancements included upgrading the armor plating, weapons, engines, sensors, and sensor jammers (the jammer that Solo installed was so powerful that the first time the unit was tested, it disrupted the information relays ''inside'' the ''Falcon'' itself, just as an Imperial corvette was launching. Luckily for Solo, the system was so powerful that it jammed itself and shut down. Solo managed to escape without notice).<ref name="Rebel Dawn">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref>

Solo's first mission with the ''Millennium Falcon'' was a trip to [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] for the benefit of his [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] co-pilot, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]. Proceeding from there, the ''Falcon'' left Imperial Space for the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], smuggling goods for crime bosses like [[Big Bunji/Legends|Big Bunji]] and [[Ploovo Two-For-One/Legends|Ploovo Two-For-One]]. As a result of its less-than-legal activities there were frequent run-ins with the [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]]. Its captain was responsible for destroying the secret Authority prison installation, [[Stars' End/Legends|Stars' End]], as well as helping to expose a slave trade ring that involved some very prominent Authority executives, in addition to participating in the ill-fated search for the lost treasure of [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]]. After its return from the 'Sector, the ''Falcon'' continued its work smuggling goods (mainly [[Spice/Legends|spice]]) for [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. Just a few months prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Solo was forced to jettison his [[3207D|cargo]] of [[Glitterstim/Legends|glitterstim]] when he was boarded by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperials]].

Around this time, [[Urai Fen]] of the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]] hired the crew of the ''Millennium Falcon'' to pick up [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Tyber Zann]] from the [[Spice mines of Kessel/Legends|spice mines]] of [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]] under the guise of a spice run. After retrieving Zann from Kessel, the crew continued their attempts to repay Jabba for the spaced load.<ref name="EAW:FC">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref> The ''Falcon'' was later snagged by the [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] of a Star Destroyer while she visited [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], but the [[Sundered Heart/Legends|''Sundered Heart'']] was able to help free the ship and, in return, Solo agreed to take the ''Falcon'' to the [[Vergesso Asteroids/Legends|Vergesso Asteroids]] in order to complete a vital mission where he dueled with [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] and the [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']].<ref name="EAW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref>

One time, the crew of the ''Millennium Falcon'' was contracted to bring supplies to [[Firebase Alpha]], an illegal energy-mining station in the [[Rishi Maze/Legends|Rishi Maze]]. Solo and Chewbacca successfully evaded a Star Destroyer and flew into the Rishi Maze. Once inside, they were attacked by a set of drones launched by a derelict [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Warship/Legends|warship]]. The ''Falcon''{{'s}} computer was able to interact with the warship's engines, and fired them into the drone fleet, disabling them. After receiving landing clearance from Firebase Alpha, Chewbacca discovered an energy signature coming from the cargo bay. Solo pried open the container and discovered they were carrying an Imperial [[Baradium/Legends|baradium]] bomb. The inside locks to the cargo bay had been damaged during the fight with the drones, so they could not jettison the bomb. Solo then put on a spacesuit so he could open the bay from the outside. His suit became damaged during the attempt, but he got the door open. Chewbacca flew the ''Falcon'' into a spiral to jettison the cargo, and came back to pick Solo up just as his suit ran out of air. The two then planned on dropping off the cargo and returning to Mos Eisley to talk to the man who had given them their cargo.<ref name="Maze Run">{{InsiderCite|131|Maze Run}}</ref>

===A Fateful Trip===
{{Quote|You came in that thing? You're braver than I thought.|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] upon seeing the ''Millennium Falcon'' for the first time|<ref name="ANH" />}}
The ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} destiny as a tool for a small-time smuggling operation was changed when it was chartered by [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] only months later for passage to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].
[[File:HanInDockingBay94-ANH.png|thumb|left|200px|The ''Falcon'' in [[Docking Bay 94/Legends|Docking Bay 94]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], shortly before departing for [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].]]
When challenged by Obi-Wan about his ship's speed, Solo cited that the ''Falcon'' was capable of attaining 0.5 past [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]], and that it "made the [[Kessel Run/Legends|Kessel Run]] in less than twelve [[Parsec/Legends|parsecs]]".<ref name="ANH" />

The journey to Alderaan proved to be much more than a simple passenger flight. The ''Falcon'' was forced to blast its way out of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] when a garrison of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] attacked the ship in an attempt to recover its cargo. It also narrowly avoided capture by a couple of [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] before making the jump to lightspeed.<ref name="ANH" />

The ''Falcon'' emerged from hyperspace into the [[The Graveyard|remains of Alderaan]]. After chasing a single [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighter]] stranded in what appeared to be empty space, the ''Falcon'' was captured by one of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star's]] [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beams]] and secured aboard the massive space station. Thanks to quick thinking by those aboard the ''Falcon'', the ship was made to appear as if the crew had escaped soon after taking off from [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. It was searched by stormtroopers and it was reported that there were no passengers on-board. Their search had managed to miss the crew, who were hidden in a series of secret smuggling holds and then proceeded to kill a scanning crew before they could be detected by the scanner.<ref name="ANH" />

[[File:AvengerChaseFalcon-ST.jpg|thumb|left|180px|''Millennium Falcon'' pursued by an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] and 5 [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]]]]

In a matter of hours, the ''Millennium Falcon'' had once again escaped the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], this time with the rescued Princess [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] onboard. After a fleeing battle with Imperial fighters and a trip through hyperspace, the ship arrived at the secret Alliance base on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. During the ship's stay on the battlestation, the Empire had planted a homing device onboard the ''Falcon'' which it used to pursue the Princess to this location. As the Rebels scrambled to organize a preemptive attack on the massive ''Death Star'', Solo loaded his reward on board the ''Falcon'' and departed the moon. However, thanks to Chewbacca, its [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] captain had a change of heart. Solo and his ship returned just in time to cover Luke Skywalker in his last-ditch effort to destroy the station and secure the safety of the Rebel Alliance. The ship's surprise attack destroyed Darth Vader's two wingmen and sent Vader himself spinning off into space, allowing Luke to successfully complete his attack and destroy the Death Star.<ref name="ANH" />

===After Yavin===
During the period between Yavin and Hoth, Han (along with [[Renegade Squadron/Legends|Renegade Squadron]]) used the ''Falcon'' to find the Holocron over the asteroid field that was once Alderaan. In its search, the ''Falcon''{{'s}} power converter and energy cell were damaged by a squadron of [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE interceptors]] and a nearby [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]]. After the encounter in the Alderaan system, the ''Falcon'' and the Mon Calamari Cruiser of Renegade Squadron entered the junkyard planet of Ord Mantell. With the necessary repairs done, Han and the rest of Renegade Squadron escaped the planet before a local Star Destroyer squadron turned up. Finally, the ''Falcon'' served as an escape transport from [[Boz Pity]].<ref name="BF:RS">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]''</ref> The ''Falcon'' also had been tracked by the Empire for their role in the Battle of Yavin.<ref name="Workshop Manual" />

===Escape from Hoth===
{{Quote|Punch It!|Han Solo to Chewbacca|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:SWM14-RoguesAndVillainsCoverArt.png|thumb|left|300px|The ''Falcon'' is pursued into the Hoth asteroid field.]]
In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the ''Falcon'' was undergoing repairs in the main hangar of the Rebel installation [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] as the Empire began its assault on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. As the Alliance scrambled to escape the base, Solo and Chewbacca hurried to make the ship spaceworthy. Princess Leia was cut off from her [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|transport]] by a tunnel cave-in and was forced to make her escape from Hoth on board the ''Falcon'' accompanied by Han, Chewbacca and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]. Solo used the ship's uncanny maneuverability and his piloting skills to elude an Imperial Star Destroyer chasing them, and two more emerging from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. Han's maneuvers in the ''Falcon'' caused the two Star Destroyers approaching and the one pursuing to nearly collide with each other. The ''Falcon'', in order to create an opening to escape due to their escape route being cut off, also disabled an already damaged Star Destroyer.<ref name="Rebel Strike">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref> The ''Falcon'' then attempted to make the jump into [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]], but was stopped short by an equipment malfunction. Forced to take drastic measures to avoid capture, Solo made the decision to pilot the ''Falcon'' into a nearby [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|asteroid field]] in an attempt to lose the Imperial pursuers. However, a near disastrous encounter with a [[Exogorth/Legends|space slug]] forced the crew of the ''Falcon'' to exit the asteroid field into the firing range of the [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']]. Han then used the [[landing claw]] of the ''Falcon'' to attach to a blind spot on the conning tower of the Star Destroyer. Adhering to standard Imperial procedure, the Star Destroyer ejected all scrap and garbage before entering hyperspace. Han then signaled Chewbacca to release the claw, allowing the ''Falcon'' to "float away with the rest of the garbage". Boba Fett, however, saw through this ruse, and waited behind in the ''Slave I'', following the ''Falcon'' as it left the system.<ref name="ESB" />

[[File:FalconLandsAtPlatform327-TESB.png|thumb|right|250px|The ''Falcon'' lands at [[Platform 327/Legends|Platform 327]] on [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]].]]
After its close encounter with the Empire, the ''Falcon'' journeyed to [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin's]] [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]], where Han's old acquaintance, Lando Calrissian, held the position of Baron Administrator. The Empire had arrived first, however, due to Boba Fett tailing the ''Falcon'' to Bespin. The crew of the ''Falcon'' were captured, tortured, and detained. Han was encased in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] and given to the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]. The remaining members of the crew, joined by Lando, escaped to the ''Falcon''. After rescuing Luke, who was dangling from a weather vane on the underside of Cloud City, the ship left the planet and attempted to jump to lightspeed. The crew were unaware that the recently repaired hyperdrive had been disabled by Vader's men, and only a last minute patch by [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] prevented the ''Falcon'' from falling into Imperial hands. Thanks to R2's efforts, the hyperdrive was activated and the ''Falcon'' managed to make the jump at the last second and escape.<ref name="ESB" />

===Rescuing Han===
{{Quote|I used to own this ship. I'll figure out a way around what Han has done to her. The man ought to be ashamed of himself.''"<br />"''I'll mention that to him when we get him out of the carbonite.''"<br />"''So will I. High, loud, and repeatedly.|Lando Calrissian and Luke Skywalker|<ref name="SoE">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>}}
During the following months, the ''Falcon'' served as home base to Leia, Luke, and Lando as they tracked Fett in an attempt to save Solo. The ''Falcon'' flew through dangerous canyons on the spaceport moon of [[Gall/Legends|Gall]], and, despite being one of the most wanted Rebel ships in the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], managed to infiltrate [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]]. It then participated in the [[Battle over Coruscant|space battle]] at [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor's]] [[Falleen's Fist|personal]] [[Skyhook/Legends|skyhook]]. After the battle, the ''Falcon'' returned to the Alliance's secret base.<ref name="SoE" /> After [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon|successfully rescuing Han]], the ''Falcon'' rendezvoused with the Rebel Fleet, and prepared to assault the newest [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="ROTJ" /> By this time, the ''Millennium Falcon'' had won the [[Superior Service Award]], the [[Legion of Merit]], the [[Valor Under Fire Citation]], the [[Combat Victory Accreditation]], and the [[Meritorious Service Award]], as well as incorporating parts from [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]], [[Cygnus Spaceworks/Legends|Cygnus Spaceworks]], and [[Taim & Bak/Legends|Taim & Bak]].<ref name="SpecPlate" />

===Battle of Endor===
{{Quote|Look, I want you to take her. I mean it, take her! You need all the help you can get; she's the fastest ship in the fleet!|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] to [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]|<ref name="ROTJ" />}}
[[File:Endorbattle.jpg|thumb|left|140px|The ''Falcon'' leads the starfighter attack during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].]]
During the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Lando and [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] copilot [[Nien Nunb/Legends|Nien Nunb]] flew the ''Falcon'' as Gold Leader. After the planetary shield protecting the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] was destroyed, the ''Falcon'' and several Alliance fighters entered the battle station through a conduit port and headed towards the reactor core. Space was limited in the conduit tunnels leading to the core and the relatively large ''Falcon'' lost its sensor dish when it smashed into a bulkhead. Lando was able to pilot the craft into the energy core housing the main reactor, launched a volley of [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missiles]], and headed for the exhaust port. The ''Falcon'' barely succeeded in outrunning the massive explosion that destroyed the powerful battlestation. Soon afterwards, the Imperial fleet retreated and the galaxy celebrated the death of the Emperor.<ref name="ROTJ" />

===New Republic===
{{Quote|According to the official records on file with Coruscant control, the ''Falcon'' is now a nice, normal light stock freighter. All of the illegal weapon systems and smuggling hardware removed. Except Han never did get around to removing all the handy little modifications and add-ons and military-specification sensors and weapons.|Lando Calrissian in 18 ABY|<ref name="Ambush">''[[Ambush at Corellia]]''</ref>}}
After the Battle of Endor, the ''Millennium Falcon'' was one of the few ships left in fighting condition that was able to drive back the invasion of the [[Ssi-ruu]]k at the [[Invasion of Bakura]].<ref name="TAB">''[[The Truce at Bakura]]''</ref> Shortly after that, it participated in the [[Battle for the Eclipse|Battle for the ''Eclipse'']], ironically against [[Tyber Zann]]'s forces. During the battle, it suffered much damage and was forced to escape into hyperspace.<ref name="EAW:FC" /> In the years following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the ship fought in the [[Liberation of Kashyyyk/Legends|Liberation of Kashyyyk]], of [[Liberation of Kessel|Kessel]].<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

[[File:Millennium_Falcon_Lightning_Gun.jpg|thumb|left|The ''Falcon'' after being modified with a [[Lightning gun (Ganath)|lightning gun]].]]

The cobbled-together nature of the ship presented many problems throughout its smuggling days and during the Rebellion. Systems were barely held together and apparently had many incompatibilities, resulting in numerous malfunctions. Years after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Han Solo and Chewbacca resolved these difficulties, much to the relief of Leia Organa Solo.

In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], Han used the ''Falcon'' to kidnap [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. Having won the deed to the planet [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] in a sabacc game, his plan was to win her heart by presenting her with the planet as a gift. He also wanted to get Leia away from the Prince [[Isolder]] of the [[Hapes Cluster/Legends|Hapes Cluster]] who was courting her. The ''Falcon'' was captured by the Imperial garrison stationed on Dathomir, after a nasty crash ''inside'' a poorly maintained [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] and then a "happy" landing on the planet, and later stolen back by Han and was pivotal in disabling the [[Super-class Star Destroyer|Super Star Destroyer]] [[Iron Fist (Executor-class)|''Iron Fist'']], killing Warlord [[Zsinj]] in the process.<ref name="Courtship">''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]''</ref>

Shortly after the events on Dathomir, Han and Leia were married and used the ''Falcon'' on a mission to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] to recover the [[Shadowcast]] intelligence code hidden on the [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[Moss painting/Legends|moss painting]] ''[[Killik Twilight]]''. They concealed the ship in an old smugglers hideout where it remained hidden until the completion of the mission.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" />

[[File:FalconEscapesChimaera-DFR5.jpg|thumb|220px|The ''Falcon'' is liberated from the belly of [[Chimaera/Legends|''Chimaera'']] by Skywalker, Karrde and Jade.]]
In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], Han and Chewie flew the ''Falcon'' to Kessel, on a diplomatic mission for the New Republic. However, on their arrival in the system, they were attacked by the [[Doole's defense fleet|Kessel mercenary fleet]] and the ship crash landed on Kessel. Han and Chewie were enslaved and sent to work in the spice mines, while the ship was repaired and pressed into service with the fleet. The ship was later liberated by Lando, though Han, [[Kyp Durron]] and Chewie nearly destroyed the ship with the [[Sun Crusher]] before finding out that Lando had taken over the ship.<ref name="Jedi Search" /> Soon after, Lando disputed the validity of the sabacc game in which Han had originally won the ''Falcon'' from him, leading to a series of rematches between them. In the first, Lando won the ship back from Han and started an attempt to upgrade and rationalize the ''Falcon''<nowiki/>'s computer systems. It was not quite finished when, in a second game, Han won the ship back. In a final game&mdash;which both men agreed would be their last rematch over the ''Falcon''&mdash;Lando won the ship back again, but, in a public attempt to impress Mara Jade, gave the ''Falcon'' back to Han.<ref name="Dark Apprentice novel">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref>

In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], the ''Falcon'' was seen in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], during [[Jaden Korr]]'s [[Mission to Mos Eisley (Disciples of Ragnos crisis)|mission to Mos Eisley]]. The ship sustained no damage during the conflict.]<ref name="Jedi Academy">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref>

Before the [[Black Fleet Crisis]] in [[16 ABY/Legends|16 ABY]], the ship was rebuilt by a New Republic team over several months. The ship was stripped down to its basic spaceframe with deformed members replaced. Then it was rebuilt from the ground up. New technology was augmented to improve efficiency; the electronics were properly grounded and pulse-shielded, mechanicals shock-mounted, cables bundled and tagged, and other parts documented and labeled. Roughly 15% of its structural parts were replaced and it weighed 300 kilograms less. The ship's [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]], [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]], [[shield lense]]s, lower [[deflector emitter]]s and [[Hyperdrive motivator/Legends|hyperdrive motivator]] were all upgraded and recalibrated. The crew quarters and holds were recarpeted, the [[sanitizer]] was recharged, and a [[YT-1300 battery regulator]] was duplicated from Corellian specs. A [[Sienar Systems augmentor]] was also installed and the missing escape pods were replaced.<ref name="Before the Storm" />

Han, to [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca's]] exasperation, was aghast at how perfect his ship performed and how smoothly it operated, declaring that he would need to go and 're-loosen' some of the nuts and bolts again, so he could tell when the ship was straining. Han was known for "flying by feel" and dialing down the inertial compensators to 95% instead of the usual 99-100% that most pilots used. This technique, he said, helped him to feel the condition of the ship better despite it sometimes catching newer passengers off guard with the unexpected G-forces being exerted during flight.<ref name="Before the Storm" />

===Yuuzhan Vong War===
{{Quote|It's not me. The navicomputer has itself convinced that trouble is the ''Falcon''{{'s}} default preference!|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] to [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]]|<ref name="Unifying Force">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref>}}
After [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca's]] death at the beginning of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Han Solo gave the ''Falcon'' a matte-black surface coating, Han said this was to disguise it, but Leia wondered if it was also in mourning for his co-pilot and best friend. During this time Han Solo rescued a [[Ryn/Legends|Ryn]] named [[Droma]] on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]], and for a short period of time, Droma became the first co-pilot of the ''Millennium Falcon'' after the death of [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]. Eventually [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] became the new co-pilot, a role she would embrace. Han Solo replaced the massive co-pilot's chair that previously belonged to Chewbacca, to make things more comfortable for Leia. Han and Leia escaped Coruscant in it during the [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|Fall of Coruscant]].<ref name="Star by Star">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref>

During the war, the ''Falcon'' performed well as usual, helping the New Republic, and eventually the Galactic Federation of Free Alliances, develop methods for effectively destroying Yuuzhan Vong Coralskippers. Anakin Solo realized that, by adjusting the angles of the quadlasers so that they were on slightly intersecting courses, when they hit a coralskipper at least one laser would penetrate the skipper's [[dovin basal]] defensive field.

Han and Leia later flew it from [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] to [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]] in the Imperial Remnant, to make a deal with the Empire to gain old Imperial maps of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]. They were looking forward to have some time alone together during the long journey and asked Leia's Noghri bodyguards to stay behind. However, their plans were ruined as they were forced to take Commander [[Vana Dorja]] with them. During the journey, they were pulled out of hyperspace by Yuuzhan Vong mines on the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]]. They were [[Skirmish on the Hydian Way|attacked]] by coralskippers and were able to fend most of them off, before [[Jagged Fel]] and his squadron arrived to help them.<ref name="Destiny's Way">''[[The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way]]''</ref>

[[File:Falcon-SAG.jpg|thumb|left|180px|The ''Falcon'' over [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].]]
About three months later, the ''Falcon'' participated in the [[Battle of Ebaq]]. Han was given command of a Smuggler's Alliance squadron and he used the ''Falcon'' as his flagship, despite [[Booster Terrik]] offering him the use of the ''[[Errant Venture/Legends|Errant Venture]]''.<ref name="Destiny's Way" />

Han Solo and Leia Organa Solo used the ''Falcon'' as a base of operations as they re-established communication checkpoints throughout the galaxy.<ref name="Force Heretic I" />

The ''Millennium Falcon'' later participated in the Second Battle for Coruscant. [[Thorsh]] was saved by the crew of the ''Millennium Falcon'' near the end of the war.<ref name="Unifying Force" />

===Second Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|Artoo reports that all hatches are sealed and all ship systems are functioning at optimal efficiency."<br />"''Optimal?'' Did we board the wrong YT? ''[...]'' Optimal ''everything'' just isn't the ''Falcon''.|C-3PO and Han Solo|<ref name="Abyss" />}}
[[File:Millennium_Falcon.jpg|thumb|The ''Millennium Falcon.'']]
By the time of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], the ''Falcon'' (now in its centennial year) was in need of engine repairs. While attempting to land on Coruscant, the engine vibrations began to shake the ship apart. Even with Han and Leia piloting, the ship was on the verge of crashing. Leia used the Force to try and slow their descent, but lacked the fine control to do so. However, with Jacen remotely bolstering her abilities with his own, Leia was able to hold the ship together for a safe, but rough landing. The ship was out of commission for the next few weeks while R2-D2 slowly repaired it.

During the battle in the skies over Hapes, the ''Millennium Falcon'' attempted to avoid combat with Leia Solo at the helm. Jacen Solo, believing that his parents were terrorists and had set him up, ordered the ''Anakin Solo'' to open fire on the ''Falcon'' (under the [[Transponder code/Legends|transponder codes]] for a ship known as the ''Longshot''). A single long range turbolaser blast was fired, destroying the central core and gun turrets of the ''Falcon''. Unfortunately, the two Noghri [[Cakhmaim]] and [[Meewalh]] were inside the turrets when they were destroyed. The ''Falcon'' managed to escape, but with serious damage.

The ''Falcon'' was repaired in the [[Gyndine/Legends|Gyndine]] system at the [[Tendrando Refueling and Repair Station]] with new turrets and central core. The ''Falcon'' later participated in the [[Battle of Kashyyyk (Second Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Kashyyyk]], [[Battle of Centerpoint Station (Second Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Centerpoint Station]], and the [[Battle of Uroro Station|Battle of Shedu Maad]] and survived them.

In the aftermath of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] and their granddaughter [[Allana Djo Solo|Allana]] went on a mission to investigate the ''Falcon''{{'s}} origins after Allana found a mysterious object on board. The three discovered an old failed plot to overthrow [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. The mission began when Allana, exploring the ship, discovered an old mechanical device with mimetic properties. Subsequent investigation led them to discover it was put into place by a former owner who had been a member of a group dedicated to restoring [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] honor. Although in a coma, the man, [[Tobb Jadak]], awoke, whereupon he joined the crew to seek the original symbol of the Republic, which had been mounted in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. The device hidden on-board was the key to finding it. When they stopped at [[Taris/Legends|Taris]], they met the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Seff Hellin]], the first Jedi to fall victim to [[Abeloth]]'s summonings. They eventually located a planet in the Unknown Regions where the Republic symbol was stored. The temple started to collapse after they learned the symbol was a fake. The former owner along with Jadak and his partner, [[Flitcher Poste]], then parted ways with the Solos to pursue the real symbol.<ref name="Falcon" />

The Solos would continue to use the ''Millennium Falcon'' as a mobile home when they assisted Luke Skywalker during his exile from Coruscant. They would respond to a distress call from him on Dathomir.<ref name="Backlash" />

==Layout and modifications==
{{Quote|Modified. Heavily modified. ''Illegally'' modified.|[[Hound's Tooth/Legends|''Hound's Tooth's'']] computer, scanning the ''Millennium Falcon''|<ref name="The Prize Pelt: The Tale of Bossk">{{StoryCite|story=The Prize Pelt: The Tale of Bossk|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref>}}
[[File:MillenniumFalconInterior.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Interior layout of ''Millennium Falcon'']]
Under the ownership of both Lando and Han, the ''Falcon'' underwent countless modifications and rebuilds. Lando had hidden cargo sections installed under the ''Falcon''{{'s}} deck plates that proved to be crucial. They provided both Lando and Han easy storage for their smuggled cargoes and hid the crew when the ship was captured by the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]]. Lando also increased the ship's shields and installed a pair of smaller [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] on the bow mandibles.

The ''Falcon'' featured [[Duralloy/Legends|duralloy]] plating over most of the vital areas of its hull and a sheet of armor plating from the [[Liquidator (Imperial II-class)|''Liquidator'']] aft of the starboard docking arm. In addition, the ship was equipped with a set of advanced [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]], [[Novaldex/Legends|Novaldex]], and [[Nordoxicon/Legends|Nordoxicon]] [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generators]] "liberated" by Solo from the [[Myomar/Legends|Myomar]] shipyards. These shield generators gave the ''Falcon'' warship-grade shielding, allowing it to survive laser hits that would destroy an ordinary YT-1300. A set of high-grade sensor suites were tied into the ''Falcon''{{'s}} oversized rectenna sensor dish. Powerful [[Sensor jammer/Legends|sensor jammers]] also protected the ship in combat.

[[File:Falcon-lounge.png|thumb|left|250px|The ''Falcon''{{'s}} main hold]]

In an effort to reduce his expenses and maintain his privacy, Solo modified the ''Falcon'' so that most of its major systems could be accessed through the cockpit or the engineering station in the main cargo hold. The myriad ship-control functions were funneled through what was once a [[Hanx-Wargel/Legends|Hanx-Wargel]] [[SuperFlow IV/Legends|SuperFlow IV]] computer. It was since modified with three [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brains]], which caused the ''Falcon'' to have [[Schizophrenia|schizophrenic]] arguments with itself, although the brains nonetheless worked together during emergencies. The droid brains were cannibalized from a military-issue [[R3-series astromech droid/Legends|R3-series astromech droid]], a [[V-5 transport droid/Legends|V-5 transport droid]], and a corporate espionage slicer droid.

The ''Falcon''{{'s}} unkempt interior matched her dilapidated exterior. The interior corridors were littered with all sorts of mechanical gear. The main hold contained a lounge area with a [[Dejarik/Legends|holographic game table]], installed at Chewbacca's request. In addition to the hidden cargo holds under her deck plates, it had a cargo-jettison feature. The ''Falcon'' lacked a [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]], and to make up for it, was equipped with a [[cryogenic hibernation capsule]]. This could be used to transport live cargo or to keep the critically injured stable until acceptable medical facilities were reached.

[[File:Falcon_smuggling_compartment.png|thumb|right|250px|The ''Falcon''{{'s}} smuggling compartments]]

The ship was frequently required to make a quick escape, and had a remarkably quick start-up time of about three minutes.

The cobbled-together nature of the ship presented many problems throughout her smuggling days and during the Rebellion. Systems were barely held together and apparently had many incompatibilities, resulting in numerous malfunctions ([[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] commented that he wasn't quite sure where the ship learned to communicate, though he may have meant that the ship's computer used slang and/or vulgar language, thus upsetting his sensibilities). Years after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Han Solo and Chewbacca resolved these difficulties, which may have involved a virtual rebuild of her internal operation systems; this was never discussed in detail.

The ''Falcon''{{'s}} customized Class 0.5 hyperdrive was twice as fast as Imperial warships, mostly due to Solo's innovative modifications to "streamline" the ship for hyperspace jumps. A Quadex power core and jury-rigged components ensured a three-standard-minute start-up sequence for the hyperdrive.

The engine block on the ''Falcon'' was designated 229811-B.<ref>[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>

===Armaments===
[[File:Falcon_egvv.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The ''Falcon''{{'s}} schematics]]
The ''Falcon'' was equipped with a pair of dorsally and ventrally mounted [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] [[AG-2G quad laser cannon/Legends|AG-2G quad laser cannons]], which drew their power directly from her [[Quadex/Legends|Quadex]] power core. Lando originally installed them to replace the mandible-mounted blasters. When Han took ownership of the ''Falcon'', he modified the cannons extensively by adding enhanced powercyclers, high-volume gas feeds, and custom laser actuators. This increased the cannons' output to the point where they could destroy a TIE Fighter with a single shot. These cannons, though typically manually operated, could be remotely accessed and controlled from the cockpit. Solo once found himself in need of this capability during the [[Blockade of Kashyyyk (1 ABY)|Blockade of Kashyyyk]] in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]. In addition, the pilots could call on the ventrally mounted, concealed, anti-personnel repeating blaster cannon near the loading ramp.

[[File:EotE_Core_Rulebook_FC_BG_art.png|thumb|right|300x300px|The ''Falcon'' in a firefight]]
A pair of [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd]] [[ST2 concussion missile/Legends|ST2]] [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missile]] launchers&mdash;illegal for a civilian to possess&mdash;were mounted between the forward mandibles. These were used in the Battle of Endor, destroying the reactor core of the second [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]]. The concussion missile launchers were modified to incorporate four concussion missiles from a variety of manufacturers, including Arakyd and [[Dymek concussion missile/Legends|Dymek]].

After becoming the diplomatic courier ship for the Skywalker-Organa-Solo family, the ''Falcon'' was refitted with military-grade power generators, propulsion, and weaponry. The quad blaster cannons were replaced by light [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]]. The turbolaser turrets were destroyed by the Star Destroyer [[Anakin Solo (starship)|''Anakin Solo'']]{{'s}} long-range turbolaser in one shot under a false transponder code ''Longshot'' during the Battle of Hapes in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]]. The turbolaser turrets were then eventually replaced with newer light turbolasers.

During the events surrounding the reborn [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor Palpatine]], the missile launchers were temporarily replaced by a giant [[Ganathan]] [[Lightning gun (Ganath)|lightning gun]] mounted in place of the portside bow mandible, which was destroyed in a shoot-out with Boba Fett's [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']]. Han didn't particularly like the modification to his ship and was quick to return the ''Falcon'' to normal once the troubles with the reborn Emperor had ended.

===Other elements===
{{Main|Freight-loading external rover}}
[[File:Cargo_Handler.jpg|thumb|200px|The ''Falcon''{{'s}} F-LER]]
Like other ships of its class, the ''Millennium Falcon'' occasionally used the freight-loading external rover (F-LER), which was commonly found at the front of the ship.
{{Clear}}

===The secrets to her speed===
{{Quote|What a piece of junk!''"<br />"''She'll make point five past lightspeed. She may not look like much, but she's got it where it counts, kid. I've made a lot of special modifications myself.|Luke Skywalker and Han Solo|<ref name="ANH" />}}
[[File:MillenniumFalconCrossSection-SWICS.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A cross-section of the ''Millennium Falcon'']]
The most famous attribute of ''Millennium Falcon'' was her [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]]. It was fully twice the size of the hyperdrive in a standard YT-1300 freighter. This system gave her a hyperdrive class of 0.5, which was twice as fast as most [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] warships. The secret to her speed was master starship tech [[Klaus Vandangante/Legends|"Doc" Vandangante's]] modifications that "streamlined" the ship in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] by controlling the warp of the space-time continuum around her. Several other ships have tried to match the ''Falcon''{{'s}} speed without these "streamlining" modifications and have blown themselves into space dust.

Another key element to the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} speed was its [[Navigation computer/Legends|navicomputer]], which could locate the quickest route from Point A to Point B while still avoiding obstacles such as star systems and [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] fields.

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Millennium Falcon'' was a recurring element in the ''Star Wars'' franchise. Its design was derived from various World War II planes, more specifically the [[Wikipedia:Boeing B-29 Superfortress|Boeing B-29 Superfortress]].<ref name="From World War to Star Wars: The Millennium Falcon">{{SW|url=news/from-world-war-to-star-wars-the-millennium-falcon|text=From World War to ''Star Wars'': The ''Millennium Falcon''|date=2014-02-18|int=From World War to Star Wars|nolive=1}}</ref>

===In the films===
[[File:ManyMillenniumFalcons-TSWA.jpg|thumb|200px|The ''Falcon'' went through many early production designs.]]
The original model for the ''Millennium Falcon'' was changed at the last minute because it too closely resembled the ''Eagle'' Transporter ships used in the [[Wikipedia:Space: 1999|''Space: 1999'']] television series by Moonbase Alpha. The replacement is said to be based on a half-eaten hamburger next to an olive on a toothpick held by [[George Lucas]], which led to staff at [[Industrial Light & Magic|ILM]] referring to the ''Falcon'' as "the Porkburger".<ref name="FSoFaF">''[[Famous Spaceships of Fact and Fantasy]]''</ref> Ralph McQuarrie's original design was modified to become the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|Blockade Runner]] starship seen at the beginning of Episode IV, and the original design was also used for the diplomatic transport that brings Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi to Naboo at the beginning of Episode I.

The cockpit design of the ''Millennium Falcon'' is heavily based on the design used in the famous B-29 Superfortress, and its flight sounds were derived from a slowed down version of a P-51 ''Mustang'' fighter recorded during a race at the Mojave Desert. World War II modeling kits can also be identified on certain parts of its shooting model.<ref name="From World War to Star Wars: The Millennium Falcon" />

[[File:MCQ-bay94.jpg|thumb|200px|[[Ralph McQuarrie]] concept art of the ''Millennium Falcon''.]]
For [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], the exterior set of the ''Falcon'' that was built for the [[Docking Bay 94/Legends|Docking Bay 94]] and Death Star scenes consisted only of the starboard half of the ship, presumably due to physical space limitations and/or financial considerations. The omission is evidenced by the absence of the sensor dish in the [[Docking Bay 94/Legends|Docking Bay 94]] scene, where it should be clearly visible. This version of the ''Falcon'' lacks the forward starboard- and port-side landing pads, which were added for [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] to better support the weight of the full ''Falcon'' exterior set that was constructed for that film. In the position where the forward starboard landing pad would later be added, a weight-bearing support (disguised as a fuel hose) is visible descending from the underside of the ''Falcon'' to the ground in both of the ''A New Hope'' docking bay scenes.

Han Solo's famous comment that the vessel "made the [[Kessel Run/Legends|Kessel Run]] in less than twelve parsecs" comes off a little incongruous&mdash;a [[Parsec/Legends|parsec]] is a measure of distance, not time (In the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|original novelization]], Solo uses the phrase "standard timeparts" instead of "parsecs"). In the 4-DVD Special Edition of the original trilogy, George Lucas explains that the remark meant that the ''Falcon''{{'s}} computer was so advanced that it was able to plot a shorter route through hyperspace than any other ship, and thus travel faster. An alternate explanation is that Solo was trying to impress his travelers with plausible-sounding yet meaningless bragging (it should be noted that while Han says this, the camera does cut to Obi-Wan looking rather skeptically at him, and the original script supports this). The Expanded Universe provides the explanation that faster hyperdrives can safely pass closer to gravity wells without deactivating, and thus the ''Falcon''<nowiki/>'s speed allowed it to fly a much shorter route than other ships.

[[File:Episode_3_Falcon.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The ''Millennium Falcon'', then the ''Stellar Envoy'', was seen docking on Coruscant [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']].]]

It was speculated that the ''Falcon'' would make an appearance in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']] to further tie the [[prequel trilogy]] to the [[original trilogy]], and the ship did indeed make a cameo in the movie. At the beginning of one shot closing in on a docking bay on Coruscant, a YT-1300 freighter is seen flying in to dock. Lucas confirmed that it was the ''Millennium Falcon'' itself and not just some other YT-1300 freighter.<ref name="SWArchive-Episode III Easter Egg Hunt: Ships Aplenty">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/bts/production/f20050526|text=Episode III Easter Egg Hunt: Ships Aplenty}}</ref>

===In the Expanded Universe===
Like many science fiction spacecraft, the ''Falcon''{{'s}} interior sets cannot actually physically fit within the exterior sets. Subsequent Expanded Universe plans are consequently a compromise attempt at squeezing the interiors in (often with detriment to headroom). These compromise plans often also result in the ''Falcon'' having rather small engines for a ship considered notable for its speed.

<!--LENGTH NOTES, see talk page also-->
This has led to some inconsistencies in the reported length of the vessel in different ''Star Wars'' publications. ''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]'' ([[2003]]) states that the ''Falcon'' is 26.7 meters long. In [[August]] [[2008]], ''[[Star Wars Blueprints: The Ultimate Collection]]'' gave the length as 35.37 meters<ref name="Blueprints" /> while the [[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']] novel, published in [[October]], gave the length to be 35 meters.<ref name="Falcon" /> The [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|StarWars.com Encyclopedia]], updated in [[September]] [[2011]], stated a length of 34.75 meters, which is the same as that of stock YT-1300 freighters.<ref name="Workshop Manual" /> The most recent publication to give a length of the ship, the ''[[Millennium Falcon Owner's Workshop Manual]]'', published in the UK in [[November]] 2011 and in the US in [[February]] [[2012]], gives a measurement of 34.37 meters. As there is no agreement on this measurement, this article uses the length from the most recent source, the ''Owner's Workshop Manual''.

[[File:Millennium_Falcon_plans_-_HOPE_watch_case.jpg|left|thumb|An alternate interior layout of the ''Millennium Falcon''.]]

In ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'', the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} power core was stated to be the same as that of the B-wing starfighter used by the Rebel Alliance. [[Paul R. Urquhart|Paul Urquhart]] elaborated on this claim in part 12 of Jason Fry's Endnotes for the book by stating that they were made by the same manufacturer and thus possessed similar components, but were not identical drives, citing the development of the USS ''Zumwalt'' and its use of the same engine as that of the Typhoon fighter jets in the British Air Force as an example.<ref name="endnotes 12">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/25364458982/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-12|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 12|quote=The claim that the power core is the 'same as that used by the Millennium Falcon' is intended to illustrate the power of the design, and references the fact that both have been attributed to the same manufacturer, and so can be envisaged as having a lot of common components. But it shouldn't be read as indicating that they use identical drives with the same serial number and completely interchangeable parts. For comparison, the USS Zumwalt, the U.S. Navy's major new surface warship, uses what's technically the same engine as the Typhoon fighter jets of the British Royal Air Force - but obviously, the version that turns propellors and drives a 500-foot destroyer up towards 40 mph is very different from the one that jets a small aircraft past the speed of sound.}}</ref>

In ''[[Tyrant's Test]]'', Chewbacca states that the quad-lasers aboard the ''Falcon'' are "large-bore [[Dennia]] quads", designed originally as crew-served weapons aboard [[Dreadnaught/Legends|''Dreadnaughts'']]. This would seem to contradict the presence of the Corellian-manufacture AG-2G cannons; alternatively, Dennia might have been the subcontractor who built the AG-2Gs.

''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]'' features the ''Falcon'' using weapons not normally attributed to it, such as ion cannons and proton torpedoes in addition to the normal quad laser cannons and concussion missile launchers. ''[[Champions of the Force]]'' in [[Star Wars: The Jedi Academy Trilogy|The Jedi Academy Trilogy]] also has the ''Falcon'' using proton torpedoes against the [[Death Star prototype]] near [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]].

[[Star Wars (1977) 50|''Star Wars'' (1977) 50]], from 1981, says that Lando Calrissian is the "original owner of the ''Millennium Falcon''".<ref name="Marvel 50">[[Star Wars (1977) 50|''Star Wars'' (1977) 50]] {{C|page 5}}</ref> This is overturned by the 1983 novel ''[[Lando Calrissian and the Mindharp of Sharu]]'', which states that Lando won what he termed the "rather elderly" ship not too long before that novel began.<ref name="LCFO" />

The ''Millennium Falcon'' also appears throughout the [[2001]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''. It may be destroyed in the Battle of Endor alternate-historical simulation in the Darth Vader campaign.

The ''Falcon'' was re-imagined in [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO]] form for the [[2006]] video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'' (based on the model released by [[the LEGO Group]] in 2004), as well as in its [[2007]] [[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|compilation re-release]].

In the video game ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'', the ''Millennium Falcon'' makes a non-canon cameo appearance. When the main character, [[Galen Marek]], finds the fourth of a series of [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]] on "Imperial [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]]," returning to the main platform on that game level allows the player to view a ship resembling the ''Falcon''. It can also be viewed on the first visit to Raxus Prime in the game, near a hyperdrive core.

Although the ''Millennium Falcon'' is technically a freighter-class capital ship, various video games, including the ''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'' games, allow the player to play as the ''Millennium Falcon'' as if it were a starfighter.

Some novels have [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] Han Solo's "parsec" boast to mean that the ship was so fast Captain Solo was able to hug closer to the black hole cluster known as [[Maw Cluster/Legends|The Maw]] without being pulled in, shaving off distance (and thus time).

====Non-canon content====
In addition to the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} appearances in the Expanded Universe, it also made some non-canonical appearances as well, including the ''LEGO Star Wars'' series of games as well as the Tag & Bink comics.

It also was the focus of the non-canon Dark Horse Comics serial "[[Into the Great Unknown]]," where it, some time after the Battle of Endor, had warped into an [[Earth system|unfamiliar star system]] and crash-landed on a [[Earth/Legends|planet]] with forests resembling that of Endor. Solo ended up killed by the natives while Chewbacca stood guard over the ''Falcon'', also becoming the legendary beast Sasquatch. 126 years later, the [[Archaeology/Legends|archaeologist]] [[Doctor/Legends|Dr.]] [[Indiana Jones]] discovered the wreck, which he had noted surpassed everything he had seen in prior expeditions, even that of [[Atlantis]], but decided to leave it to the great unknown alongside Sasquatch.

===In the real world===
In February 2007, the LEGO Group announced the release of the Ultimate Collector's ''Millennium Falcon'', scheduled for [[October 1]] [[2007]].<ref name="LegoMF">{{LEGOWeb|subdomain=shop|url=ByTheme/Product.aspx?p=10179&cn=416&d=322|text=Ultimate Collector's ''Millennium Falcon''}}</ref> The model is scaled to LEGO Minifigures, measuring 33" long by 22" wide. At 5,195 pieces, it is the second-largest LEGO Set ever produced, and the most expensive.

[[Hasbro]] released what is known to fans as the "Big ''Millennium Falcon''" toy on July 26th, 2008. When the original Kenner mold for the toy broke down after 30 years of use, Hasbro brought in the original designer of the toy, Mark Boudreaux, to redesign the iconic ship. The completed product is approximately 30% larger than the Kenner version.<ref name="BMF">{{Rebelscum|url=story/euro/BMF_The_Official_Press_Release_115770.asp|text=BMF: The Official Press Release!|author=Curto, Dan|date=2008-07-02}}</ref> It can hold up to 18 figures.

In the ''[[Star Wars: Where Science Meets Imagination]]'' traveling exhibit, a reproduction of the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} cockpit is featured within a miniature planetarium.

===In non&ndash;''Star Wars'' works===
[[File:AkiraFalcon-STFC.jpg|thumb|200px|The ''Millennium Falcon'' fights with the [[MemoryAlpha: United Federation of Planets|Federation]] in the [[MemoryAlpha: Battle of Sector 001|Battle of Sector 001]].]]

A CG model of the ''Falcon'' was inserted in the battle in the film [[Wikipedia:Star Trek: First Contact|''Star Trek: First Contact'']], engaging the {{MA| Borg Cube|Borg cube]] with the rest of [[MemoryAlpha: Starfleet|Starfleet]], the military arm of the [[MemoryAlpha: United Federation of Planets|United Federation of Planets]]. [[John Knoll]] of [[Industrial Light & Magic]], which did the special effects for the film, as well as having just completed work}} begins its first attack against the cube in the early stages of the battle, and just before an [[MemoryAlpha: Akira-class|''Akira''-class]] starship is destroyed.

[[File:Star_Wars_Easter_Egg_The_Dig_1.gif|thumb|right|200px|''Millennium Falcon'' and Star Destroyer Easter Eggs in ''The Dig''.]]
In [[Wikipedia:The Dig (video game)|''The Dig'']], a point-and-click adventure game released by LucasArts in 1995, several light bridge control panels bear "alien designs" carved into them, including some that appear to be ''Star Wars'' [[Easter egg (virtual)|Easter eggs]]. One such panel features simplified line drawings of the ''Millennium Falcon'' and a Star Destroyer of unknown classification.

A YT-1300 freighter, similar to the ''Millennium Falcon'', can be seen for a second on the landing platform of the Space Diner in the Mel Brooks space parody, [[Wikipedia:Spaceballs|''Spaceballs'']].

In the ''Star Wars'' spoof [[Wikipedia:Blue Harvest|Blue Harvest]], when Peter, who plays Solo, says that the ''Falcon'' made the Kessel run in under twelve parsecs, Luke, played by Chris, questions him, saying "Um, isn't a parsec a unit of distance, not time?". Solo blows him off in response.

Similar to how [[w:c:pirates:Jack Sparrow|Jack Sparrow]] from [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]]'s ''[[w:c:pirates:Pirates of the Caribbean|Pirates of the Caribbean]]'' franchise was compared to Han Solo, the ''[[w:c:pirates:Black Pearl|Black Pearl]]'' was compared to the ''Millennium Falcon''. It was said at least once by [[Wikipedia:James Ward Byrkit|James Ward Byrkit]], a creative consultant of [[Wikipedia:Gore Verbinski|Gore Verbinski]]'s ''Pirates'' trilogy, in the [[Disney+]] series ''[[Wikipedia:Prop Culture|Prop Culture]]''.<ref name="Prop Culture">{{DisneyPlus|url=series/disney-prop-culture/3vXywewCCYr5|text=Prop Culture|archivedate=20200515070401|quote=And so, the Black Pearl, we needed it to feel very different than the others. It's haunted, it's a special place. Wherever you look, you feel like you're being watched. This idea that the sails actually had personality to it, the way they were ripped, they almost had faces coming out. And yet, it's Jack Sparrow's Millennium Falcon. You know? It's his ship that he loves so much. So you have to not hate it, you actually have to think it's kind of beautiful.}}</ref> [[A. C. Crispin]] spoke of how she was privileged to write the scene where Han first beheld&mdash;and fell for&mdash;the ''Millennium Falcon'' in ''[[Star Wars: The Han Solo Trilogy|The Han Solo Trilogy]]'', and assured fans it was every bit as thrilling to write the scene with Jack Sparrow and the merchant ship ''Wicked Wench'', which was later renamed ''Black Pearl'', when releasing the fifth excerpt of ''[[w:c:pirates:The Price of Freedom|Pirates of the Caribbean: The Price of Freedom]]''.<ref name="TPoF Excerpt 5">{{WebCite|url=http://www.accrispin.com/The%20Price%20of%20Freedom%20excerpt%2005.pdf|text=The Price of Freedom excerpt 05.pdf – Chapter 6|author=[[A. C. Crispin|Ann Crispin]]|date=2011-03-15|format=PDF|archivedate=20110903052943}}</ref>
